title: Getting started without code
standfirst: “No code” covers three separate jobs: creating a machine, running an agent on it, and keeping it running. A provider can be good at one and bad at the others, and the difference is usually a terminal.

concept.heading: Three jobs, often confused
paragraphs: Creating a machine is the first job. Several providers now let you do it from a dashboard with a button: InstaBox, Lizard, Runtime and Boat all have some version of it. Running an agent is the second job, and it is where most “no-code” claims break. A preinstalled agent is not a hosted agent: you still open a terminal and type a prompt, or call an API.

Keeping it running is the third job, and it is where a personal agent lives or dies. A dashboard that can create a sandbox but not set an always-on schedule has not solved the problem a non-technical buyer actually has.

concept.heading: The rise of “hand it to your agent”
paragraphs: The most common no-code path in late 2026 is not a wizard. It is a prompt. Runtime tells you to paste its `llms.txt` link into Claude Code or Cursor. boxd's sign-in page offers to copy a prompt for your AI agent. Sandboxer hosts an MCP server you add as a connector in Claude or ChatGPT. Boat lets an agent sign itself up through `auth.md`, with a human claiming the account and entering the card.
That works well for someone who already has a coding agent and is comfortable delegating. It is not the same as a product where a non-technical person clicks “start” and gets a working assistant.

concept.heading: What to check before signing up
paragraphs: Three practical questions sort providers quickly. Do I need a card before I can see anything? Sandboxer, Boat and Lizard say yes; Runtime says no; Agent 37's personal free plan says no. Is there a prebuilt agent, and who pays for the model? Only Agent 37's managed hosting and Boat's preinstalled harnesses come close, and both still bill the model separately or through your own account. And is there a status page and a support channel that is not one founder's inbox? Several providers in this set have neither.

comparisonIntro: Can someone who does not write code get from a website to a working agent, and what still needs a terminal?

rows.note: The managed-hosting line is genuinely one-click (OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code and others, with a task board and desktop, no card on the free plan). The Cloud API, which this site mostly compares, has no documented click-to-create flow.

source.quote: Run OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Grok around the clock. Yours is live in one click.

rows.note: The dashboard is a control panel: sandbox list, countdown, terminal, desktop, billing. Every documented workflow is a CLI command, and a card is required before the first sandbox. The one no-code route is adding its MCP server to Claude or ChatGPT.

source.quote: You need a card on file before you can start a sandbox.

rows.note: CLI-first: install, log in, create. The sign-in page offers to copy a prompt for an AI agent, and the desktop is point-and-click once a machine exists, but nothing creates a first machine from the website alone.

source.quote: Or hand it to your clanker: copy the prompt

rows.note: The dashboard creates a machine from a template with a button, opens a Linux desktop you can click, publishes ports and saves snapshots. There is no hosted agent: you type your request into Claude Code or Codex in the box's terminal.

source.quote: In the dashboard, **Create machine** on the **Machines** page does what `instabox create` does.

rows.note: The dashboard creates sandboxes without code — template, region, size and lifetime — with a browser terminal. Running an agent, taking a snapshot, forking or attaching a volume are CLI or SDK only.

source.quote: The dashboard lets you create and manage Sandboxes without code.

rows.note: One click starts a sandbox with a shell, but there are no app templates and no hosted agent; the documented no-code path is pasting its `llms.txt` link into Claude Code or Cursor.

source.quote: sign in and press **Start a sandbox** on Home. It opens with a shell running in the page

rows.note: The dashboard shows sandboxes, opens the desktop and manages billing and AI sign-ins, but creating and prompting a sandbox is `boat new` then `boat prompt`. No wizard, no gallery.

questions: Can I create the first machine from the website, without a terminal?
Is there a prebuilt agent, or only an empty Linux box?
If there is a prebuilt agent, who pays for the model — the provider, or my own account?
Can I see and drive the desktop from a browser?
What do I need before I start: a card, an invite, a coding agent?
When something breaks, who do I ask, and is there a status page?

picks.situation: A personal agent today, without touching a terminal
picks.why: Managed hosting is the only product here that starts at $0, needs no card on the free plan, and gives you a working agent with a task board and desktop. Everything else in this set assumes a terminal somewhere.

picks.situation: I am happy to paste one prompt into Claude or ChatGPT
picks.why: All three document that path: Sandboxer hosts an MCP server, Runtime publishes an `llms.txt` to hand over, and Boat lets an agent sign itself up. You still need to check what the agent did.

picks.situation: I want to click around a real Linux desktop
picks.why: Each has a dashboard-created machine and a browser desktop. InstaBox and Lizard create the machine from a form; boxd expects the CLI first and then gives you the desktop.

picks.situation: I want to learn what a sandbox is by poking at one
picks.why: Runtime gives free hours with no card and a one-click shell. Lizard's dashboard creates a sandbox with a chosen lifetime, though its trial needs a card.

picks.situation: A team that will need SSO and an audit trail
picks.why: Runtime includes SSO, SCIM and audit logs free. InstaBox and Lizard put them on their Enterprise tiers. Agent 37 and Boat publish nothing on SSO.

gotchas: Sandboxer's seven-day trial becomes a $20-a-month plan automatically on day eight.
Lizard needs a card to start its trial; Runtime does not.
A preinstalled agent is not a hosted agent: you still pay the model provider or sign in with your own subscription.
Agent 37's $5 Cloud credit needs a card, while its personal free plan does not.
Several providers have no status page, so an outage looks like a broken account.
